# Figures: Skills Map

<!-- Generated by `npm run figures:docs` from src/components/figures/catalog.ts. Edit the catalogue, then run it again. -->

Which part of the map is this? Links back to the Skills Map: an animated emblem for each territory and chips for the skills a section used.

How to add one to an entry, and the rules they all follow: [figures.md](../figures.md).

In this file: [TerritoryMark](#territorymark) · [Territories](#territories) · [Skills](#skills)

## TerritoryMark

`A-01` · A territory with its animated emblem, its question and a link to its page.

**Use it for**

- The opening of a section that belongs to one territory: "How I measured" under Measurement.
- Case study and interview: the part of the map the work was about.

**Not for:** More than two in one entry. For several territories at once use Territories.

**Skills Map:** territories discovery, strategy, experience, engineering, shipping, measurement, activation, retention, distribution, operations, ai, cross-cutting

**Motion:** reveal, ambient, interactive

**Props**

- **`territory`** *(required)* `string`: A territory id: discovery, strategy, experience, engineering, shipping, measurement, activation, retention, distribution, operations, ai, cross-cutting. The name, question and counts are read from the Skills Map.
- **`note`** `string`: One line on what this section does in that territory.

It has no frame, so it takes none of the frame props.

**Example: Measurement**

```mdx
<TerritoryMark
  territory="measurement"
  note="This section: the events, the split and what I decided before looking."
/>
```

**Example: Discovery**

```mdx
<TerritoryMark
  territory="discovery"
/>
```

**Example: Retention**

```mdx
<TerritoryMark
  territory="retention"
/>
```

**Example: AI**

```mdx
<TerritoryMark
  territory="ai"
/>
```

## Territories

`A-02` · The twelve territories as emblems, with the ones a piece of work touched lit and counted.

**Use it for**

- Case study, "My role" or "Outcome": how wide the work was.
- The end of a long entry: which parts of the map it used, at a glance.

**Not for:** Repeating the map at the top of the entry. Use it when the spread across territories is the point.

**Skills Map:** territories cross-cutting; skills `professional-development`, `reflection`, `system-dependencies`

**Motion:** reveal

**Props**

- **`skills`** `string[]`: Skill ids. Their territories are lit, with the number of skills in each. Usually the `skills` of the entry. Inside a profile, each lit territory links to the section that covers it.
- **`territories`** `string[]`: Territory ids to light, when there is no list of skills.
- **`all`** `boolean`: Light all twelve.

Plus the frame props: `title`, `caption`, `evidence`, `source`.

**Example: From the skills of an entry**

```mdx
<Territories
  title="Where the first-session experiment sat on the map"
  skills={[
    'drop-off-analysis',
    'first-run-flows',
    'hypotheses',
    'signup-flow',
    'frontend-development',
    'ab-tests',
    'sample-size',
    'retention-curves',
  ]}
/>
```

**Example: All twelve**

```mdx
<Territories
  all
/>
```

## Skills

`A-03` · The skills a section used, as chips that link to their pages and show the reader’s own status.

**Use it for**

- Under a section heading or after a figure: the two or three skills that part of the work exercised.
- With `route`, the order the work went through them.

**Not for:** Listing every skill of the entry: the page already does that beside the map.

**Skills Map:** territories cross-cutting; skills `professional-development`, `updating-beliefs`

**Motion:** none

**Props**

- **`ids`** *(required)* `string[]`: Skill ids, in the order the work used them. An unknown id fails the build.
- **`label`** `string`: The label in front. Default "Skills used here".
- **`route`** `boolean`: Join the chips with arrows, when the order matters.
- **`labelHref`** `string`: Makes the label a link, to a territory page or a section.
- **`labelCode`** `string`: A catalogue code before the label, such as a territory's 01.
- **`notes`** `Record<string, string>`: One sentence per skill id, shown on hover instead of the skill's summary.

It has no frame, so it takes none of the frame props.

**Example**

```mdx
<Skills
  ids={['funnel-analysis', 'drop-off-analysis', 'hypotheses']}
/>
```

**Example: As a route**

```mdx
<Skills
  label="In this order"
  route
  ids={['user-interviews', 'hypotheses', 'ab-tests', 'interpreting-results']}
/>
```
